name: Laquatus
description: A merman and ambassador of the Mer Empire who controls Turg and schemes to obtain the Mirari.

description_citations.text: "Turg". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer gives a dark gift to a darker soul for Laquatus's champion.
timeline.quote: Chainer's dark gift to a darker soul.

citation.text: Laquatus's Champion (Torment, 2002), flavor text. Wizards of the Coast.

timeline.summary: Balthor and Kamahl are ambushed in Krosa by Cabalists and Order Legionnaires under Laquatus.
timeline.quote: they were ambushed by Cabalists and Order Legionnaires under the influence of Ambassador Laquatus

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "A New Home". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Cabalists raise Balthor as a zombie, Balthor the Defiled, who hunts Laquatus.
timeline.quote: The Cabalists raised him as a zombie

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "Balthor the Defiled". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus controls Balthor and forces him to fight Kamahl; Balthor begs to be killed and Kamahl does so, then kills Laquatus.
timeline.quote: Balthor begged Kamahl to end his suffering

citation.text: "Balthor Rockfist", section "Balthor the Defiled". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus rewrites Kirtar's memory, sowing false alliances.
timeline.quote: Laquatus, ever the manipulator, had rewritten his memory

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar flees to the Order's lands, pursued by Kamahl and Laquatus.
timeline.quote: Kirtar fled back to the Order lands, pursued by Kamahl and Laquatus

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Aboshan seizes the Mirari; his plan to flood Otaria ends in his death and the creation of the Aboshan Trench.
timeline.quote: His genocidal designs to flood Otaria culminated in his death

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus's forces are trapped by Empress Llawan's magics.
timeline.quote: Laquatus’ forces collapsed into oblivion, trapped by the widowed Empress Llawan ’s cunning magics

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl and Jeska are led into the Krosan Forest by Balthor Rockfist, pursued by the Cabal and Order remnants and Llawan's armies.
timeline.quote: Kamahl and his mortally wounded sister ventured into the Krosan Forest

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In Krosa, Laquatus's alliance collapses as Seton's druids resist and the undead Balthor hunts Laquatus.
timeline.quote: The alliance collapsed under its treacheries

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl embraces the druids' teachings and drives a sword through Laquatus into Krosa's soil, ending the battle but leaking the Mirari's influence into the soil.
timeline.quote: He plunged the sword through the body of Laquatus and into the forested ground of Krosa.

citation.text: "Battle for the Mirari", section "Description". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids leads Cabalists to the Mer Empire capital and makes a deal with Laquatus to find the Mirari; Aboshan finds it first and dies.
timeline.quote: she made a deal with Laquatus to find the Mirari for him

citation.text: "Braids", section "To the Mer Empire". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids hunts Kamahl with five serpent assassins, who slaughter many but are killed by barbarians.
timeline.quote: killed all five of her snakemen

citation.text: "Braids", section "In league with the Patriarch". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids zombifies Balthor in revenge for Leer and sets him against Laquatus before teleporting away.
timeline.quote: Braids then zombified Balthor in revenge for him killing Leer

citation.text: "Braids", section "The capture of Jeska". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Braids, Traybor and Eesha reveal Laquatus's treachery and leave him alone in Krosa.
timeline.quote: leaving the merman alone in the forest

citation.text: "Braids", section "The capture of Jeska". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer creates Burke for Laquatus and heals Kamahl with snakeskin; Kamahl burns his skin off, ruining their friendship.
timeline.quote: His refusal to accept the Cabal's gifts ruined his and Chainer's friendship.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer uses the Mirari to power a Death Bloom that kills the Patriarch's guards, forcing the Patriarch into exile in Aphetto, and takes control of Cabal City.
timeline.quote: he took control of Cabal City and, therefore, fulfilled the Mirari’s visions.

citation.text: "Chainer", section "Dementist". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl, Seton and Laquatus leave after Kirtar, who has the sphere; Chainer resumes training under Skellum.
timeline.quote: Chainer resumes his training as a dementia summoner under his master Skellum

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mirari returns to the First, who makes it the prize of the Cabal Anniversary Games; Chainer and Kamahl train as a duo; Llawan claims the throne of the seas.
timeline.quote: Aboshan's wife Llawan claims the throne of the seas

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus starts a civil war in the Mer Empire and schemes with both Order and Cabal; the First sacrifices Skellum in the pits, devastating Chainer.
timeline.quote: In his plotting, he sacrifices Skellum, who dies in the pits to appease them.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer completes his initiation in Krosa with Kamahl and becomes a full dementia summoner able to master the Mirari; he creates Burke for Laquatus.
timeline.quote: he becomes a full-fledged dementia summoner.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer disarms the First, fails to kill him, banishes him to Aphetto and takes control of the Cabal, showing signs of corruption.
timeline.quote: He, therefore, banishes him to Aphetto

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Games become a show for Chainer; he loses control of dementia creatures, who overrun the city; he draws them into himself and is corrupted, and makes Kamahl promise to take the Mirari.
timeline.quote: makes Kamahl promise to take it and keep it safe, away from misuse.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus's army is defeated in the Aboshan Trench and Llawan's mages trap him in a bubble; he swears revenge.
timeline.quote: Llawan's mages create a bubble that entraps him and what remains of his followers in it.

citation.text: "Chainer's Torment", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus and Eesha try to obtain the Mirari while Jeska and Balthor try to separate it from Kamahl for fear of its corrupting influence.
timeline.quote: attempt to obtain the potent orb for themselves

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: After politics and war, the Mirari, attached to Kamahl's sword, is implanted through Laquatus's corpse into the Krosan Forest, channeling its magic into the land.
timeline.quote: is implanted through the corpse of Laquatus and into the Krosan Forest

citation.text: "Judgment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus, trapped by Llawan's mages and failing diplomatically with the Order and the Cabal, goes to the mainland with Burke to retrieve the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Laquatus and his jack Burke go personally to the mainland to retrieve the Mirari

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: An Order contingent led by Eesha and a Cabal battalion led by Braids head to the mountains while Laquatus plays them against each other.
timeline.quote: Laquatus tries to play them against each other while pretending to be a friend of both.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: At the forest's edge Balthor holds off the pursuers and unleashes a great spell that kills himself and Burke; Laquatus discovers his troops were wiped out by Llawan's and forges a flimsy alliance with the Cabal and Order.
timeline.quote: the dwarf unleashes a great spell that kills them both.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: An unknown assailant attacks the camps in the forest and the Order leader is killed, blamed on the Cabal, which leaves.
timeline.quote: An unknown assailant begins to attack the camps, and the Order leader is killed, but the blame is given to the Cabal.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Eesha, Braids and Llawan's envoys reveal Laquatus's plotting and abandon the quest for the Mirari, leaving him without support.
timeline.quote: They decide to leave the former ambassador to his own devices and abandon the quest for the Mirari.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl discovers the assailant is Balthor, zombified by Braids, and ends his undeath in tears.
timeline.quote: he is Balthor, zombified by Braids and instructed to kill Laquatus.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills Laquatus with the Mirari sword, its power now bringing growth and peace, and the forest is rejuvenated.
timeline.quote: The merman dies pinned by the sword.

citation.text: "Judgment (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kirtar uses the Mirari to crystallize much of the Order's fortress, including himself and Captain Pianna; Laquatus ends up with the Mirari.
timeline.quote: Kirtar used the device to cast a devastating spell that crystallized much of the fortress

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Kamahl's Odyssey". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Attacked at the edge of the Krosan forest, Balthor sacrifices himself so Kamahl can flee with Jeska; Seton guides Kamahl in and Thriss teaches him druidism.
timeline.quote: Balthor chose to sacrifice himself to let Kamahl flee with Jeska.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus mind-controls zombified Balthor into fighting Kamahl, who is forced to strike down his old mentor at Balthor's plea.
timeline.quote: Balthor begged Kamahl to end his torment, and so Kamahl was forced to strike down his old mentor.

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl strikes down Laquatus with the Mirari-sword, leaves it in the ground and forsakes the Mirari for a druidic life.
timeline.quote: With that act, Kamahl forsook the Mirari and his violent past

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Redemption in Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl meets Karona, then resolves she must be stopped; he retrieves the Mirari from Laquatus's corpse with Balthor's ghost's help.
timeline.quote: it was only through Balthor's spiritual sacrifice that Kamahl managed to gain control over the Mirari-sword

citation.text: "Kamahl", section "Karona's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: A Krosan dragon attacks the city, Kirtar leads the defense, and Kamahl kills the dragon, leaving Kirtar to receive the reward.
timeline.quote: Eventually, Kamahl killed the dragon

citation.text: "Kirtar", section "Pit fighter". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus, who had implanted false memories of friendship, joins Kirtar, and Pianna orders Kirtar and his men to withdraw.
timeline.quote: She ordered Kirtar and his men to withdraw back to the Order's citadel.

citation.text: "Kirtar", section "The Battle for the Mirari". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Through Laquatus's treachery the Otarian merfolk lose most of their empire to the cephalids.
timeline.quote: the merfolk lost much of their Mer Empire to the cephalids due to Laquatus 's treachery

citation.text: "Merfolk", section "Otarian Merfolk". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Turg gives the Mirari to Captain Satas, who takes it to Emperor Aboshan.
timeline.quote: Turg gave the Mirari to Captain Satas

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Discovery". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl kills Laquatus in Krosa and leaves the Mirari-sword in the ground.
timeline.quote: Kamahl finishing the merman by driving the Mirari-sword through Laquatus and into the ground

citation.text: "Mirari", section "Krosa". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Mer Empire schemes for absolute control by flooding the continent and killing the "inferior air-breathers".
timeline.quote: scheme for absolute control of the continent by flooding the continent and killing the "inferior air-breathers"

citation.text: "Odyssey", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus reaches Kirtar at the Order encampment; Pianna demands the sphere and Kirtar plots a coup.
timeline.quote: The aven reluctantly complies but plots a coup

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus returns to the Mer capital and stokes Aboshan's fears as Llawan challenges his rule; Kamahl settles in Borben.
timeline.quote: Llawan , the estranged empress, appears to challenge Aboshan's rule.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus and Fulla stop Aboshan at the cost of Turg's life and take the Mirari to Cabal City.
timeline.quote: Laquatus and Fulla manage to stop him before the damage is too great, at the cost of Turg's life.

citation.text: "Odyssey (novel)", section "Plot". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl has just slain Laquatus with the Mirari sword, causing vegetation to flourish around it.
timeline.quote: Kamahl has just slain Laquatus using the Mirari sword.

citation.text: "Onslaught (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Pianna travels to Krosa when Kirtar slaughters the forest's animals and orders him to withdraw.
timeline.quote: Pianna ordered Kirtar to withdraw his remaining men back to the citadel

citation.text: "Pianna", section "Confronting Kirtar". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kamahl, guided by Balthor's ghost, retrieves his sword from Laquatus's corpse and defeats the giant Laquatus again.
timeline.quote: Kamahl has to defeat his old nemesis again

citation.text: "Scourge (novel)", section "Summary". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus's treachery lets Aboshan's cephalid empire take over the waters around Otaria.
timeline.quote: his treachery allows Aboshan and his cephalid empire come to take over the rule the waters around the continent of Otaria

citation.text: "The Secrets of Magic", section "Stolen Harvest , by Vance Moore". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Chainer discovers the Mirari and rises through the Cabal, rivaling the Patriarch before his fall; Kamahl befriends him and Laquatus plots to seize the Mer Empire.
timeline.quote: Chainer's Torment presents the tale of Chainer , a Cabal dementia summoner, discovering the Mirari and rising through the ranks of the Cabal

citation.text: "Torment", section "Flavor and storyline". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Turg is captured and psychically grafted to Laquatus, becoming more intelligent.
timeline.quote: rigorously trained to be Laquatus's servant by being psychically grafted to the merman

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Turg eats a Krosan dragonette, whose call draws a full-grown dragon to devastate Cabal City.
timeline.quote: Turg was partly responsible for causing the devastation of the city

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Turg first fights Seton and Kamahl while Laquatus pursues Kirtar across Otaria's northern plains.
timeline.quote: Turg briefly fought them but withdrew at Laquatus's command

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Turg wrestles Seton in Krosa and blinds him nearly with vomited acid before retreating.
timeline.quote: Turg vomited on Seton's face and retreated

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: At the Order's citadel, Turg fights Kamahl, then takes the Mirari from Kirtar but mistakenly hands it to Satas.
timeline.quote: Turg then mistakenly gave the orb to Satas

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Laquatus makes himself central to Aboshan's court and uses Turg to arrest and frame his enemies.
timeline.quote: Laquatus maneuvered to make himself central to the court under the pretext of rooting out traitors

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Aboshan finds the Mirari in the vaults and prepares to flood Otaria; Laquatus and Turg fight the guards.
timeline.quote: Aboshan decided to inspect the vaults, where he found the Mirari

citation.text: "Turg", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.
